newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BNP-DRESDNER BANK HUNGARY UNIT BUYS SECURITIES HOUSE.
newsitem.headline: BNP-DRESDNER BANK HUNGARY UNIT BUYS SECURITIES HOUSE.

text.p: BNP-Dresdner Bank (Hungaria) Rt said on Wednesday it had completed its search for a brokerage house in Hungary by acquiring a 90 percent stake in Budapest bourse member Arany Broker Securities house.

"BNP-Dresdner Bank today acquired 90 percent of Arany Broker," Laszlo Madarasz, General Manager of BNP-Dresdner Bank told a news conference, adding that the remaining 10 percent will be held by Arany's general manager, Gabor Lebovits.
Lebovits, who has been appointed for another three year term, declined to reveal the transaction price.
BNP-Dresdner said the acquisition will allow it to enter a new market segment.
"The purchase of Arany Broker Rt entitles the bank to develop investment banking activities," it said in a statement.
"BNP-Dresdner Securities will play an important role in the organisation of issuing securities and fund management activities."

The current 90-10 percent ownership reflects the securities house's ownership structure after a capital increase by which BNP-Dresdner raised Arany Broker's 250 million issued share capital to 500 million.
The securities house, which specialises in the trading of government papers and participates in the primary dealer system, has been renamed to BNP-Dresdner Securities.
Lebovits said the search for a bank partner was also Arany Broker's plan.
"Without a banking background one cannot develop further in the long-term," he said.
Lebovits said he expected the securities house's profitability to "substantially improve" as a result of the acqusitions and also hoped its clientele will grow.
He said he expected a turnover of 160 billion forints in 1996 but declined to give a profit forecast.
The acquisition comes at the end of almost a year's search by BNP-Dresdner for a suitable partner.
In January this year the French-German bank said it was considering buying Microbroker, a small Budapest bourse member brokerage, but talks later stopped.
The bank said in October that it was in negotiations with another broker which it declined to name.

BNP-Dresdner Bank (Hungaria) Rt, 50-50 percent owned by Banque Nationale de Paris and Dresdner Bank AG, generated a pre-tax profit of 1.1 billion forints in the first eleven months of 1996, compared to 690 million forints in the whole of 1995.
Its total assets grew to 51 billion by the end of November from 35.2 billion at the end of 1995.
